lines.text: You are at a cafe, and your coding agent, on a computer at home, starts doing something you did not intend.
On your phone you see it. The agent is about to delete a folder you wanted to keep.
In Agent R Q you open the machine session. It is a real terminal, right in your phone browser.
And there you are, at the agent prompt, watching its output live, as if you sat at the desk.
Every key goes through, escape included. The key that terminal agents need most still works on a phone.
One press, and the agent stops mid-thought, before it finishes the thing you did not want.
Then type what you actually wanted, in plain words, right into the same prompt.
The agent reads it, understands, and carries on, this time the right way.
No laptop, no remote desktop, no vpn dance. A phone and a browser are enough.
The agent still asks before risky commands, so you get an approval, and an emergency stop.
So you can leave the desk, and still be one tap from the controls.
What was the scariest thing you ever saw an agent start to do? Tell us, or try machines at Agent R Q dot com.
